title: Hillgrove, McEachern battle strength versus strength - NewsBreak
text:
By Adam Carrington ,
7 hours ago Jaiden Moore and Hillgrove will host McEachern in the annual “Battle Down in Powder Town” on Friday for at least a share of the Region 3 lead. By Cecil Copeland 2025, file Hillgrove has one of the top running backs in Cobb County while McEachern has one of the top defenses.
Friday's winner of the annual “Battle Down in Powder Town” at Hillgrove could come down to which unit has the most success. The winner of this matchup will also have a chance to stay in at least a tie for the Region 3 lead.
Hillgrove standout Jaiden Moore is second in the county in rushing yards after five games. Known for his speed in open space, Moore has 629 yards on 51 carries and five touchdowns. He's also averaging 12.2 yards per carry.
Moore is currently coming off a 156-yard effort on 17 touches against Pebblebrook two weeks ago. His 48-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter helped the Hawks hold off the Falcons 35-28.
In the previous week, Moore compiled 234 yards and two touchdowns in Hillgrove's win over Northgate. At 6-foot, 180-pounds, the senior currently holds nine Division I offers including Middle Tennessee, Miami (Ohio) and Florida Atlantic, among others.
“Jaiden has elite speed,” Hillgrove coach Justin DeShon said. “He trusts his vision and his O-line. If you give him a crease, he can get into the end zone. He makes the offense easy for you because he is fast, elusive and a heck of a weapon.” We're glad we got him.”
The Indians have been successful on the defensive side of the ball this season, yielding just 14.2 points per game.
“We're going to play our brand of football,” McEachern coach Kareem Reid said. “We haven't given up a bunch of rushing yards this year. We have our work cut out for us for sure (with Moore), but I'm confident that we can execute our game plan.
“Our defense has done a good job playing with energy and enthusiasm. We're proud of their efforts.”
Linebacker Michai Rowe is currently leads McEachern with 44 tackles and two fumble recoveries. Georgia-bound linebacker Joakim Gouda has 26 stops and two tackles for loss. Defensive end Jordan Simpson has 23 tackles and is tied for the lead with two sacks.
“The one thing that jumps our on film is that they have an abundance of talent (on defense),” DeShon said of McEachern. “The second thing that sticks out is how well coached they are. Their secondary guys are elite players. Up front, they are strong and do things soundly.”
